newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/4 to 3/8.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices end down 1/4 to 3/8.

text.p: U.S. Municipal bonds ended down 1/4 to 3/8 of a point Wednesday as players lamented limited cash flows.

"There's no cash flow at all," one trader said. "I think people are just really confused about what the next step is, and I think the minute you get any weakness like what happened today it becomes extremely illiquid."
Market sources cited outflows from municipal bond funds last week, with $669 million exiting the funds by one estimate.
On Wednesday, U.S. Treasuries showed early promise, edging up after the September Consumer Price Index came in as expected. Both the overall and core rates were up 0.3 percent.
But improvement quickly faded, leaving the government's benchmark bond down 5/8 to 3/4 of a point or more by midday. Munis were down 1/2 at midsession.
"I think everybody was set up to sell any kind of a rally," a muni trader said. "It was so short-lived, and once it went the other way, the inactivity just gets really bad."
The benchmark 30-year bond later managed to recoup some losses, closing down 7/32 at 98-19/32 to yield 6.86 percent.

A municipal analyst said high-grade issues ended Wednesday's session two basis points weaker overall, and three basis points softer on the long end. Dollar bonds ended down 1/4 to 3/8 after having been down nearly 1/2 point at noon.

Wednesday's actively quoted issues included Intermountain Power Agency, Utah, 5.0 percent supply revenue refunding bonds of July 2021. The bonds were bid at a 5.86 percent yield, up from a 5.82 yield on Tuesday.
In debt futures, the December municipal contract closed down 6/32 at 114-8/32. The December T-bond contract closed down 6/32 at 110-10/32. The MOB spread was 126 ticks.

As for new issues, Seasongood & Mayer Wednesday said it repriced Ohio's $168.8 million taxable development assistance bonds to yield 88 basis points over comparable Treasuries in the 2021 maturity. Preliminary pricing had those 2021 maturity yielding 90 basis over comparable Treasuries.

Also Wednesday, Lehman Brothers repriced $84.5 million Michigan State Housing Development Authority bonds, raising yields five basis points, and moving the top yield in 2027 to 6.20 percent from 6.15 percent.

On the competitive side, Goldman Sachs & Co said it won $100 million Port Authority of New York and New Jersey consolidated revenue bonds subject to the alternative minimum tax at a true interest cost of 5.64 percent. The offering featured a top yield of 5.8 percent in 2016.

Prudential Securities Inc won $30 million Wisconsin general obligation bonds subject to the alternative minimum tax at true interest cost of 5.93 percent. The offering featured a top yield of 6.050 percent in 2027.

Turning to Thursday's deals, eight negotiated deals totaling $549 million are expected. A $375 million New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority offering via senior manager PaineWebber Inc leads the list. An $80 million New York State Dormitory Authority offering through Bear Stearns & Co is also expected.

Thursday's scheduled competitive municipal issues are expected to total $336 million in 17 offerings. The largest issue is a $200 million Massachusetts Bay Transportation Authority offering set for 1100 EDT.
